title: A Systematic Review of Post‐2100 Climate Change
content:
Abstract

Climate services seek to inform decisions about long-term climate changes. Since the 1990s, the vast majority of climate projections have covered the period up to 2100, a horizon that is not so distant anymore. This leaves decision makers tasked with planning coastal development or building long-lived infrastructure with relatively sparse information to assess climate risks, evaluate the costs and benefits of adaptation options, and implement carbon emission mitigation actions. In a bid to better understand how climate services could extend further into the future, this paper reviews the literature to understand how and why post-2100 climate studies are conducted. It identifies three broad themes: understanding climate processes with great inertia, assessing climate risks and informing adaptation actions, and evaluating emission mitigation scenarios. Multiple papers reveal the complex interplay between climate feedbacks, and show how climate change post-2100 is not merely an extension of 21st century trends. The overwhelming focus on the current century downplays the long-term damages of current emissions and fails to convey the possibility that future climate conditions could exceed adaptation capacity. We reiterate numerous calls made in the literature to extend mainstream climate emission scenarios and climate model projections farther into the future, and provide the building blocks for robust climate products.
